subject: multilayer perceptron under Perceptron / Linear model
chosen_reading: MLP is a root; `perceptron` is a node under `Linear model`
rejected_reading: MLP (and through it most of the neural tree) sits under Perceptron, and therefore under Linear model
why_the_choice: The name carries the lineage, but the perceptron's defining content is a learning rule, which the admission rule sends to the algorithms hierarchy; the surviving model is a linear decision boundary. The modern object called an MLP is defined without reference to it.
impact_if_wrong: If wrong, every neural lineage gains a second path to `Linear model` and the level-1 cut puts ~90% of the corpus in one bucket.

subject: linear discriminant analysis
chosen_reading: a descent node under `Linear model`
rejected_reading: a node under `Mixture model` / `Directed graphical model`, since its coefficients come from class-conditional Gaussians
why_the_choice: The learned object is a linear boundary and that is what papers run; the generative parameterisation is how it is fit.
impact_if_wrong: Low. A second parent to `mixture_model` would be a cheap repair.

subject: Gaussian process (and the kernel machines generally)
chosen_reading: admitted as models; `Gaussian process` is a node
rejected_reading: algorithm-only, by the same reasoning the brief applies to k-NN and kernel density estimation
why_the_choice: A fitted GP is serialisable and runnable as a unit (hyperparameters plus the retained data) and carries a real and distinctive compute profile, which is what the dimension exists to record.
impact_if_wrong: Moderate: if GPs are algorithm-only then so is the SVM, and the whole `Kernel machine` root moves.

subject: k-means
chosen_reading: a node under `Mixture model` (the hard-assignment limit)
rejected_reading: algorithm-only, like k-NN; or a root of its own for prototype models
why_the_choice: The centroids are learned parameters and are separable from Lloyd's algorithm, so admission succeeds; the placement follows the standard reading of k-means as a degenerate GMM.
impact_if_wrong: Low. Only the placement is at risk, not the admission.

subject: recurrent networks as state-space models
chosen_reading: no edge: `Recurrent network` is a root, `State-space model` is a root
rejected_reading: `Recurrent network` under `State-space model`, and `Deep state-space model` under `Recurrent network`
why_the_choice: Elman does not define his network from state-space theory and Gu defines S4 from the continuous-time SSM, not from the RNN literature. The equivalences are retrospective.
impact_if_wrong: Moderate: a real edge here would merge two roots and change the level-1 cut for every sequence model.

subject: detection architectures (R-CNN line, YOLO, SSD, RetinaNet, DETR)
chosen_reading: nodes under their own lineage, with the backbone recorded per mention/run rather than as a parent edge
rejected_reading: a parent edge from each detector to every backbone it is ever paired with
why_the_choice: `Faster R-CNN with a ResNet-50 backbone` is a configuration, not a named release; making it an edge would make the DAG dense and would double-count every backbone.
impact_if_wrong: Low for the tree, high for compute estimation: the backbone carries most of the FLOPs, so the run record must hold the pairing.

subject: GRU under LSTM
chosen_reading: `GRU` is a sibling of `LSTM` under `Recurrent network`
rejected_reading: `GRU` is a child of `LSTM` (Cho introduces it by comparison with the LSTM unit)
why_the_choice: The GRU is fully definable on its own terms (two gates, no cell state); the comparison in the paper is positioning, not definition.
impact_if_wrong: Low. Aggregation at `Recurrent network` is unaffected.

subject: sequence-to-sequence
chosen_reading: a composite node with both `LSTM` and `GRU` as parents, placed by composition
rejected_reading: a division child of `Recurrent network` alongside the cell types; or a node under `LSTM` alone
rule_in_tension: one principle per sibling set (PROCESS rule 2)
why_the_choice: Seq2seq is a wiring of two recurrent networks, not a cell form, so it cannot join the cell-form sibling set; the brief exempts descent-produced siblings from the division principle.
impact_if_wrong: Low.

subject: Vision Transformer's depth
chosen_reading: `ViT` is a node under `Encoder-only Transformer` (depth 2)
rejected_reading: `ViT` is a node directly under `transformer` (depth 1), as the brief's worked table in 4.7 writes it
rule_in_tension: the brief's worked example vs the encoder/decoder division
why_the_choice: ViT is a stack of bidirectional encoder blocks and belongs to that division value; the worked row demonstrates R1 plus the acronym case, not an exact depth. Declared rather than resolved silently.
impact_if_wrong: Low, and reversible: the edge would simply move up one level.

subject: denoising and masked autoencoders
chosen_reading: nodes under `Autoencoder`, with the objective recorded in notes
rejected_reading: algorithm-only, with the model being the backbone, exactly as the brief rules for SimCLR
rule_in_tension: the admission rule; the SimCLR fixed point
why_the_choice: The corruption/masking is a training objective, but each names a released, separable pair of networks that the field treats as an architecture.
impact_if_wrong: Moderate: if MAE is algorithm-only then so are several SSL families, and the `Autoencoder` root loses two of its four children.

subject: GAN as a model or an algorithm
chosen_reading: `Generative adversarial network` is a root: the generator-discriminator pair is the model, the adversarial game is the algorithm
rejected_reading: GAN is an algorithm (as diffusion is), and the named GAN artifacts hang off their convolutional or transformer backbones
rule_in_tension: the admission rule; the diffusion fixed point
why_the_choice: Symmetry with `Autoencoder`: a shape made of two sub-networks in a defined relation is an architecture. Also, StyleGAN-class releases are separable learned objects by any reading.
impact_if_wrong: High for aggregation: under the rejected reading `GAN` disappears as a cut and ~25 corpus names move under CNN.

subject: word2vec's placement
chosen_reading: under `Word embedding model`, a division child of `Factorization model`
rejected_reading: under `Feedforward network`, following Mikolov's own framing as a shallow log-linear network
rule_in_tension: R1 (paper framing) vs the learned object
why_the_choice: The learned object is an embedding table looked up per token, which is what the root's characteristic names; the shallow-network reading would file word2vec beside MLP classifiers it shares nothing with at any cut.
impact_if_wrong: Low in this corpus (no word-embedding names were found at all), but it is a declared R1 violation.

subject: `large language model` / `LLM`
chosen_reading: quarantined as an uninformative generic
rejected_reading: a node under `Decoder-only Transformer`
rule_in_tension: the no-dividing-by-scale rule (MODELS_BRIEF B.2); 4.7's generics treatment
why_the_choice: What `LLM` adds to `decoder-only Transformer` is scale and use, the two things the design may not divide by. There is no `Large models` node anywhere, and this would be one.
impact_if_wrong: High in volume: `large language models` and relatives are frequent, and quarantining them removes them from family shares. The alternative is to let the second pass resolve each mention to the named release when the quote gives one.

subject: `diffusion model` and the diffusion releases
chosen_reading: `diffusion model`/`DDPM` is algorithm-side (the model is the denoiser); named releases (`Stable Diffusion`, `DALL-E`) are R5 composite nodes
rejected_reading: a `Diffusion model` family node under which all diffusion artifacts hang
why_the_choice: The fixed point is explicit: the model is the denoiser, usually a U-Net. A family node would re-admit a training procedure as an architecture.
impact_if_wrong: High in volume: ~37 corpus names contain `diffusion`; most become algorithm mentions plus a backbone.

subject: LoRA and other adapters
chosen_reading: algorithm-side (a finetuning method); the adapted model stays its parent node
rejected_reading: a node per adapted artifact, or a `Parameter-efficient model` grouping
why_the_choice: LoRA weights are not runnable independently of the base model, so there is no separable learned object; the pair (base model, LoRA) is a run configuration.
impact_if_wrong: Low for the tree; it does mean `lora` leaves this hierarchy entirely.

subject: proprietary releases with no published architecture (GPT-4, Claude, Gemini, Midjourney)
chosen_reading: admitted as nodes under the division node their vendor documentation supports, with the weak evidence recorded in notes
rejected_reading: quarantined until an architecture is published; or admitted as roots because no lineage is attested
why_the_choice: These are the most-named artifacts in a 2024-2026 corpus and dropping them would gut the dimension; the vendor's own statement is the best framing that exists. Midjourney, which has no such statement, is deliberately left for the second pass rather than guessed.
impact_if_wrong: Moderate: a wrong parent misattributes a share at the division cut, though the artifact-level count stays right.

subject: the string `lda`
chosen_reading: ambiguous: it is NOT a spelling; each mention resolves from context to `linear_discriminant_analysis` or `latent_dirichlet_allocation`
rejected_reading: a single spelling entry pointing at whichever is more frequent
why_the_choice: R3 collapses a string only when it denotes the same release; `lda` denotes two unrelated models in two different roots.
impact_if_wrong: Low if the second pass is told; silent collapse would merge a classifier with a topic model.

subject: mixture of experts
chosen_reading: `Mixture-of-experts network` is a node under `Feedforward network`; sparse MoE layers inside a Transformer are a PROPERTY of that model (Switch under T5, Mixtral under Mistral)
rejected_reading: an `MoE Transformer` grouping node under `Transformer`
why_the_choice: Sparse routing crosses the encoder/decoder division, so a grouping node would introduce a second principle into that sibling set.
impact_if_wrong: Low for structure; it does mean `mixture of experts` mentions land in the feedforward root rather than beside the LLMs.

subject: slot attention
chosen_reading: a descent node under `Transformer`
rejected_reading: a node under `Autoencoder` (it is usually embedded in a convolutional autoencoder) or under `Recurrent network` (slots are updated by a GRU)
why_the_choice: Iterative attention binding features to slots is the defining mechanism and it is attention; the surrounding autoencoder varies by paper.
impact_if_wrong: This is the least settled placement in the file. Flagged in SELF_AUDIT.

subject: the Transformer's ancestry
chosen_reading: `Transformer` is a root
rejected_reading: `Transformer` is a child of `Attentional encoder-decoder`, which its own paper names ('the Transformer follows this overall architecture')
rule_in_tension: R1 vs the brief's fixed point in 4.7
why_the_choice: The brief fixes `transformer` as a root under R6. The framing in the paper is a negation ('dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely') plus an inherited block diagram.
impact_if_wrong: High if reopened: the entire Transformer subtree would move under `Recurrent network`, which is plainly not what the dimension wants.

subject: LLM generations as siblings or as a chain
chosen_reading: `GPT-2`, `GPT-3`, `GPT-4` are siblings under `GPT`, following the brief's sketch
rejected_reading: a successor chain GPT -> GPT-2 -> GPT-3 -> GPT-4, since each is defined as a scaled continuation of the last
why_the_choice: The brief draws them as siblings and a flat generation set keeps the `GPT` cut meaningful; the chain reading would make depth grow with time.
impact_if_wrong: Low. Aggregation at `GPT` is identical either way.

subject: the string `sam`
chosen_reading: resolves to `Segment Anything` only when the quote is about segmentation
rejected_reading: a spelling entry mapping every `sam` to the segmentation model
why_the_choice: The corpus also uses `sam` for sharpness-aware minimisation and for LiDAR SLAM systems, neither of which is this node.
impact_if_wrong: Low if flagged; a silent mapping would pollute a vision family with an optimiser.

subject: the plural `transformers`
chosen_reading: a plural spelling of the `Transformer` root, EXCEPT where the quote shows a mass-noun use ('transformers have become dominant'), which is quarantined
rejected_reading: blanket quarantine, as 4.7 lists it among the generics
why_the_choice: R3's pluralisation case is explicit, and 4.7 qualifies the quarantine with 'as a plural mass noun' -- i.e. the distinction is usage, which only the mention's quote can settle.
impact_if_wrong: Low in either direction, but it must be decided once rather than per mention.

subject: GFlowNet
chosen_reading: algorithm-side: `gflownet` names the training objective and the model is the flow network the paper instantiates (an MLP, a GNN or a Transformer). No node in this hierarchy.
rejected_reading: a `GFlowNet` root (or node), since the flow network is a separable learned object with a distinctive founding idea
rule_in_tension: the admission rule; the diffusion and SimCLR fixed points
why_the_choice: Exact parity with diffusion: a network plus a procedure, where the network is whatever backbone the paper chooses. Admitting it would re-open the diffusion fixed point.
impact_if_wrong: THE highest-volume call in this derivation: ~33 corpus names contain `gflow` and the bare term is among the ten most frequent names. If the owner wants GFlowNets aggregated in the models dimension, the rule to revisit is the diffusion fixed point, not this row.

subject: application-named model classes
chosen_reading: quarantined: `species distribution model`, `epidemiological model`, `surrogate model`, `world model` name what a model is FOR, not what it is built from
rejected_reading: a node per application class
rule_in_tension: the rejected characteristic 'data structure consumed / function learned'
why_the_choice: These divide by use, which section 3 rejects at every level; papers that use them almost always also name the architecture.
impact_if_wrong: Low in count, but it is the same error v0's `classic_ml` and `others` roots made.

subject: synonyms at grouping nodes
chosen_reading: SPELLINGS.tsv carries a fourth case, `synonym`, used once (`gradient boosted trees` -> `Boosted tree ensemble`)
rejected_reading: forcing such strings into `orthographic` or leaving them unmapped
why_the_choice: R3's three cases were written for releases; grouping nodes attract synonyms rather than respellings, and that case has no slot. Declared rather than fudged.
impact_if_wrong: Low, but the spec for SPELLINGS.tsv should gain the case.
